headline: A report of a US–Iran peace framework knocked oil off a five-month high and pushed the dollar to a three-week low. The pound led the day, near $1.34 after strong UK jobs data.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar slipped about 0.2% to near 101.7 on the index, after touching its lowest since October 1. A report of a US–Iran peace framework pulled oil and long-term yields down, and two weak housing reports added to it.
chapters.meaning: What changed: three things since this morning. First, a Qatari paper reported that Qatar and Pakistan had put a framework to Washington and Tehran, with Iran getting interest on frozen funds and allowing a quiet nuclear inspection. Neither government confirmed it, and a diplomat in the talks said reports that a deal is close are wrong. Oil fell, the 10-year yield slipped about 2bp to near 5.11%, and the dollar index briefly dipped to about 101.5 before settling near 101.7. Second, housing starts, through the four beats: (1) how many new homes builders began; (2) 1.22 million at an annual rate against 1.30 million expected, down about 5%; (3) mortgage rates above 7% are biting harder; (4) for the dollar, a weaker economy argues for a slower Fed, a mild drag. Third, pending home sales, signed contracts on existing homes: down 7.3% against a small dip expected, to a record low. Same message, from the buyer side. Thread: this morning's edition said the dollar's support came from oil lifting yields, not new US strength. Today showed the reverse: when oil fell, the dollar fell with it. Yet two-year yields edged up and the December hike stayed almost fully priced, so the Fed story itself did not change. What it means: the dollar is trading as an oil-and-yields currency right now. The lens: is the Fed's December hike still the base case if oil eases?
chapters.fx: What to watch: API crude stocks 3:30 PM CT today; any US or Iranian statement on the reported framework; EIA inventories 9:30 AM CT Wednesday. The Fed stays in its quiet period until the October 28 decision.
numbers: Housing starts 1.22M vs 1.30M expected; pending sales -7.3% (record low)
Fed: Oct hold ~83%; Dec hike ~94% (CME FedWatch)

scenarios.base: If the framework stays unconfirmed and oil holds near today's levels, the dollar drifts near 101.7 with yields.
scenarios.bull: If the talks collapse or the Gulf escalates, oil and yields rise again and the dollar recovers today's loss.
scenarios.bear: If Washington or Tehran confirms the framework, oil and long yields fall further and the dollar extends toward its October lows.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro gained about 0.2% to near $1.124, helped more by cheaper oil than by Europe's own news. France delayed its budget revenue vote to October 27, and German investor morale fell more than expected.
chapters.meaning: What changed: three European items and one big outside one. France pushed the revenue vote on its 2027 budget to October 27; amendments already passed would add about €10 billion to the deficit. German ZEW expectations, through the four beats: (1) a survey of investors on the next six months; (2) 28.1 against about 30 expected, the first fall in six months; the euro-area reading dropped further to 18.5; (3) high energy prices are wearing down confidence even as current conditions improved; (4) for the euro, a softer outlook slightly weakens the case for ECB hikes. The euro area's current-account surplus collapsed to its lowest since January 2023, a sign that the big energy bill is eating the region's trade income. Against that, the US–Iran report pulled oil down, which helps an energy importer, and the euro rose to about $1.124. Thread: this morning's edition named the Paris vote as the euro's test; the test moved a week, so the French bond gap stays a live risk without a verdict. What it means: the euro's best friend today was oil, not Europe. Moody's review of France on Friday is now the next French test. The lens: does cheaper oil help the euro more than French politics hurts it?
chapters.fx: What to watch: Bundesbank's Nagel 2:15 AM CT Wednesday; Lagarde Wednesday; Moody's France review Friday; France's revenue vote October 27; ECB decision October 29.
numbers: German ZEW 28.1 vs ~30 expected; euro area 18.5
EZ current account €8.7B (Aug), lowest since Jan 2023
France revenue vote moved to Oct 27

scenarios.base: If oil stays below its highs and Paris stays quiet until the vote, the euro holds near $1.12.
scenarios.bull: If the US–Iran framework is confirmed and oil falls further, the euro gains on a smaller import bill.
scenarios.bear: If Moody's cuts France on Friday or oil jumps back, the bond gap widens and the euro slips toward last week's low near $1.111.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound was the day's best major, up about 0.5% to near $1.338 after briefly topping $1.34 for a five-week high. MPC member Greene backed the hawkish jobs reading. Wednesday's inflation report is next.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the morning's jobs beat kept paying through New York, and the dollar's slide added to it. Greene's speech, through the four beats: (1) an MPC member's view on pay; (2) she said wage growth has stopped cooling at a level still too high for 2% inflation, and that forward-looking signs point higher; (3) that is a policymaker saying the job market alone will not bring inflation down; (4) for the pound, it backs a November hike and keeps a second hike in view. The 10-year gilt auction also drew solid demand, a calm read on UK debt a week before the budget. The pound rose about 0.5% to near $1.338 after touching about $1.341. Thread: this morning's edition said the pound now leans on Wednesday's inflation report; today's gains raise the bar for that report. What it means: markets almost fully expect a November 5 hike, so what matters is whether December follows. The lens: is the BoE's next move after November a second hike or a pause?
chapters.fx: What to watch: UK inflation 1 AM CT Wednesday (about 3.4% expected); Bailey 8 AM CT Wednesday; the budget October 28; BoE November 5.
numbers: BoE Nov 5 hike almost fully priced (LSEG)

scenarios.base: If inflation lands near 3.4%, the November hike stays locked in and the pound holds near $1.34 into the budget.
scenarios.bull: If inflation runs hotter, markets price a December follow-up and the pound extends above $1.34.
scenarios.bear: If inflation surprises low, December hopes fade and the pound gives back today's gain.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The yen firmed slightly to near 158.2 per dollar, its first gain in three days. Record demand at a 20-year Japanese bond sale drew money home, and lower US long yields helped.
chapters.meaning: What changed: two pushes in the yen's favour. Tokyo's 20-year bond auction drew record demand, which pulled Japanese yields down and eased worries about Japan's debt, and State Street called it a sign that sidelined cash is coming back. Then the US–Iran report pulled oil and US long-term yields lower, which narrows the rate gap that weighs on the yen. USD/JPY dipped below 158 at one point and ended near 158.2, about 0.1% lower. Thread: this morning's edition called the yen quiet and pinned by the US–Japan rate gap; the gap narrowed a little and the yen moved a little, which fits that story. What it means: cheaper oil helps Japan twice, through a smaller import bill and lower US yields. But the move was small, and the BoJ is still seen waiting until December. The lens: is Japan's inflation strong enough to bring the BoJ's next hike forward?
chapters.fx: What to watch: Japan trade balance 6:50 PM CT tonight; Japan national inflation Friday; BoJ October 29–30 with new forecasts; 160 per dollar, where Japan has stepped in before.
numbers: BoJ Oct 30: hold expected; Dec hike likely

scenarios.base: If US yields hold near 5.1%, USD/JPY stays just under 160 into Friday's inflation report.
scenarios.bull: If oil keeps falling or Japan's inflation beats, the rate gap narrows and the yen firms further.
scenarios.bear: If oil and US yields climb again, the yen slides back toward 160, where intervention risk rises.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc firmed about 0.2% to near 0.825 per dollar as the dollar slipped. Against the euro it stays near its strongest in three months, close to where the SNB has pushed back before.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the dollar's slide did the work. USD/CHF eased to near 0.825. Against the euro, the franc held close to a three-month high as worries about French debt kept some money in Swiss assets, and Tradingpedia notes it is nearing levels where the SNB has threatened to step in. Switzerland's trade surplus came in well below forecast, but that did not move the franc. The US–Iran report took some fear out of markets, which on its own would soften a safe haven. Thread: this morning's edition said the franc moves on outside fear, not Swiss news; today it moved on the dollar instead, and outside fear eased. What it means: the franc's strength against the euro is now the SNB's problem, with zero rates leaving few tools besides selling francs. The lens: is outside fear rising faster than the SNB's patience?
chapters.fx: What to watch: the SNB's write-up of its last meeting Thursday; Moody's France review Friday; any Gulf or US–Iran headline.

scenarios.base: If France and the Gulf stay tense but contained, the franc drifts with the dollar.
scenarios.bull: If French stress spreads or the Gulf escalates, haven demand lifts the franc broadly.
scenarios.bear: If a US–Iran deal is confirmed and France calms, the haven bid drains and SNB pushback weighs on the franc.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie rose about 0.4% to near 1.406 per dollar, its strongest in about four weeks. Alberta voted by a wide margin to stay in Canada, removing a risk, and a Bank of Canada hike stays mostly priced.
chapters.meaning: What changed: two things. Alberta's first-ever referendum on leaving Canada ended with about 76% voting to stay, which takes a political risk off the loonie. And Bank of Canada pricing held: swaps put the odds of an October 28 hike at about 80–85%. The loonie touched about 1.403, its best since September 22, before settling near 1.406. It gained even as oil fell from its highs, which shows the rate story now matters more than the oil story. Thread: this morning's edition said a hike had become the base case and a hold would now be the surprise; nothing today changed that. Our call that USD/CAD would hold 1.41–1.43 into the decision broke as the loonie firmed. What it means: Canada has both a rate edge and less political risk. Hedge funds are still betting heavily against the loonie, so those bets are exposed if the hike comes. The lens: is the BoC set on acting before the data proves it?
chapters.fx: What to watch: oil and any US–Iran confirmation; Canada retail sales later this week; BoC decision October 28.
numbers: CFTC: hedge funds strongly against CAD

scenarios.base: If BoC officials don't push back on hike bets, the loonie holds near 1.40–1.41 into the decision.
scenarios.bull: If more forecasters switch to a hike, bets against the loonie get squeezed and it gains further.
scenarios.bear: If oil falls sharply on a confirmed US–Iran deal or the BoC signals patience, hike pricing unwinds and the loonie gives back the move.

chapters.teaser: The kiwi rose about 0.3% to near 0.568 with the softer dollar. The dairy auction was firm for milk powders, a plus for New Zealand's export income. Wednesday's inflation report at 4:45 PM CT decides the hike case.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the Global Dairy Trade auction, through the four beats: (1) a fortnightly auction of New Zealand's biggest export; (2) whole milk powder rose about 4% and skim milk powder about 3%, while butter, fats and cheddar fell; (3) powders are the prices that matter most for farm income, so this is a mild boost to the country's trade earnings; (4) for the kiwi, better export income adds a little support and does nothing to argue against a hike. The kiwi rose about 0.3% to near 0.568, mostly on the dollar. Thread: this morning's edition said hike odds near 80% had moved ahead of the data; the auction backed that a little. What it means: the inflation report is now the whole story. In line keeps the hike on; clearly soft would put a hold back on the table. Hedge funds are betting against the kiwi, so a hawkish surprise could force them to cover. The lens: is New Zealand's inflation cooling fast enough to let the RBNZ wait?

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Oil swung hard: Brent hit a five-month high near $112 on Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi sites, then settled down 0.7% at $108.79 after a report of a US–Iran framework. A diplomat said a deal is not close.
chapters.meaning: What changed: two stories pulled oil in opposite directions. Early, the Houthis' claims of strikes on Saudi energy and airport sites, still unconfirmed by Riyadh, pushed Brent to about $112, and Gulf stock markets fell. Then a Qatari paper reported a Qatar–Pakistan framework that Washington and Tehran had received positively, and Iran's president met Pakistan's army chief, a key go-between. US crude briefly fell near $95 before a diplomat said reports of a near deal are wrong. Brent settled at $108.79; the expiring November US contract settled at $101.79 and the December contract at $97.82. Kpler counts at least 18 ships attacked in two weeks, so the supply risk is real. Thread: this morning's edition asked whether tankers are moving through the Gulf again; they are not, but the market now sees a diplomatic exit. What it means: oil is trading on headlines both ways, which moves the loonie, the yen and US yields with it. The lens: does diplomacy move faster than the attacks?
chapters.fx: What to watch: API inventories 3:30 PM CT today; EIA inventories 9:30 AM CT Wednesday; any US or Iranian confirmation of the framework; Houthi activity near Saudi export routes.
numbers: At least 18 vessels attacked in two weeks (Kpler)

scenarios.base: If talks continue without confirmation and attacks stay at today's pace, Brent swings around $105–112 on headlines.
scenarios.bull: If Saudi damage is confirmed or talks break down, the premium rebuilds and Brent tests $112.
scenarios.bear: If either government confirms the framework or tanker traffic recovers, the premium drains quickly.

chapters.teaser: Gold slipped about 0.5% to near $4,121, a third straight loss, even as yields and the dollar eased late. It traded between roughly $4,110 and $4,155, still in the lower half of its range.
chapters.meaning: What changed: gold had two pulls. Early, oil-driven yields and firm Fed hike bets pushed it to near $4,112.
